description: EMBOSS 6.6.0 seqmatchall: the all-against-all comparison of a set of sequences by exact word matches. For every pair i < j with length(i) > wordSize and length(j) >= wordSize every maximal exact match of at least wordSize symbols is reported (forward strand only; overlapping matches and repeated positions are all listed). Nucleotide or protein sequences (any letters, compared literally and case-insensitively); the program's word table leaves out words around its unknown symbol (N for a nucleotide sequence, X otherwise) with a scan that can keep a word that holds an N after a skipped one - reproduced exactly. Positions are 0-based (the program prints 1-based starts). Matches are listed per pair, by position (the program lists them in hash order: compare as sets). Verified against seqmatchall 6.6.0 on 330 random sets (2-5 sequences, nucleotide / N / lower case / protein, word sizes 2-12, 700+ pairs); on A/C/G/T input it equals find_common_regions mode MaximalExactMatches (MUMmer -maxmatch). Input sequences are read as EMBOSS reads them (A4-3, one shared reader): only letters and '*' are kept; gap characters (- . ~ ?), '#', '+', '_', digits, blanks and every other character are dropped first, and positions, lengths and scores count the cleaned sequence (e.g. needle of AC-GTTAGC.TT* and ACGTTAGCTT: score 58, length 11, as the program). More than 4 194 304 maximal word matches are refused with an ArgumentException (SequenceAligner.WordMatchMaxMatches).

sequences.description: The sequences (at least one; nucleotide or protein letters).

sequenceQualifiers.description: EMBOSS sequence-input qualifiers as on the command line: -sbegin 3 -send -2 -sreverse -slower -supper -scircular -snucleotide -sprotein (begin / end 1-based, negative = from the end; -sreverse reverse-complements a nucleotide sequence, the range then refers to the original). Measured on EMBOSS 6.6.0 per program: seqmatchall ignores -sbegin / -send; -sreverse (taken by the whole set when its first sequence is nucleotide) only labels the sequences reversed: the words are matched on the sequences as given and numbered from the end. The result then lists the program's start / end positions (reversed: start > end) in 'reportedMatches'. The text is resolved exactly as the EMBOSS program resolves it on its command line after the sequence arguments (ACD, 6.6.0): -sbegin1 3, -sbegin1=3, -nosreverse1, -sreverse1 N, any case, -/--/ prefix, and every UNIQUE abbreviation (-sbeg1, -sre2; uniqueness is decided among all qualifiers of the program, an ambiguous or unknown one is refused). The number is the sequence (1, and 2 for the second sequence of a two-sequence program; 1 for a program with one sequence). An unnumbered qualifier belongs to the LAST sequence given (-sbegin 3 is -sbegin2 3 in a two-sequence program) until a qualifier of another sequence ends that tie; after that it applies to all sequences. -sformat selects the file format of the text; -ufo -fformat -fopenfile name the feature file of a program that takes the features of its sequences (diffseq: the files are given by the tool); -sask -squick -sdbname -sid -iquery are accepted without effect (residue strings have no file); any other qualifier or a stray word is refused.
